It has been a year since I bought fixer. I bought this from Amazon and was wondering if this is correct.

Kodak Professional Fixer with Hardener for both Black & White Film and Paper, Powder to Make 1-liter

Now when I got it, the package said it was a general purpose hardening fixer for film plates and paper.

It did not show a 7:1 dulution for paper.

Can anyone provide a link for an online source for fixer?

Thanks,

Tony

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
Hey Tony, I have never used the powdered stuff. Here is what I use and I get it from a local photography shop.

If you click the picture of it you can see on the big bottle it states to make one gallon which would be 3:1 (film and plate)and to make two gallons which would be 7:1 (paper), even though the add does not mention the 7:1. I make the 7:1.

[http://www.calumetphoto.com/item/KP02020/](http://www.calumetphoto.com/item/KP02020/)

posts.author: DJ Mathson

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
Well Tony, you could always compare MSDS of each. 

Here is Ilford

[http://www.ilfordphoto.com/Webfiles/200 ... 462739.pdf](http://www.ilfordphoto.com/Webfiles/2006118140462739.pdf)

Here is Kodak

[http://www2.itap.purdue.edu/msds/docs/9712.pdf](http://www2.itap.purdue.edu/msds/docs/9712.pdf)

It doesn't look like the Ilford had a hardener.

Hey why not just get some Sodium Metabisulfite and Alum and make your own fixer so you can tweak it to your film age, desired bandwidth and color?

In fact I have some of both I could send you some to play with if you want. The idea is if you need more hardener, just add more for your second plate.

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
DJ Mathson, ever so sorry. I must be gettting old. I've called Tony Joe a few times...LOL! Yes, I use the Kodak Rapid Fixer with Hardener (2 part and in liquid form). I have used both the one I posted and the one Danny Posted with good success. I try to get the FIxer that has the hardener separate. The important thing here is to dilute the raw stock solution 7:1 instead of 3:1. On the bottle I posted, it states that right on the front. The Sodium Metabisulfite needs a little extra tweaking but is more adaptable.

Danny, that's why you tweak it with alum.

Colin, I think you meant Jeff stated to use Potassium Dichromate instead of Ammonium Dichromate which we talked about at around the same time as the discussions about Fixer and Sodium Metabisulfite. But I could be wrong.
